confirmed.title: 通用 provider 停用/撤銷會把「全 iPhone 共用」的受器/動器一併關掉，波及未被停用的其他手機
confirmed.file: crates/interaction-runtime/src/providers.rs:1270-1272 (disable_provider_capabilities body at 1323-1358)
confirmed.claim: 本分支為修 v0.5.1 #4 新增的 `Runtime::disable_provider_capabilities`（provider.rs:1323-1358），在 `transition_provider` 對 Disabled/Closed/Expired/Revoked 一律呼叫（1270-1272），直接把 `ProviderDescriptor.receptors`/`.actuators` 逐一 `set_receptor_enabled(false)`/`set_actuator_enabled(false)`。但 iPhone 這一族的能力 id（`iphone.motion`/`iphone.battery`/`iphone.touch`/`iphone.mic-level` 與六個動器）是**跨所有已配對手機共用的全域單例**，並非每台各自一份——`mobile_register_provider`（mobile.rs:3286-3292）明白寫著「這六項不是『這一台專屬』的能力，而是所有已配對 iPhone 共用的同一組動作能力；descriptor 不得讓人以為每台各有一份」，且每支手機的 provider descriptor 都塞進完全相同的字面陣列。因此對任一支手機呼叫通用的 `interact-ai providers transition <id> --state disabled`（或 `.../revoke`）就會把**全部**已配對手機的 mic-level、haptic、通知、甚至角色呈現動器 `iphone.character` 一起關掉——包含正在串流麥克風的另一支手機，且沒有通知它、沒有幫它送停止請求、稽核只指名被停用的那一支（`provider.capabilities-disabled`/`provider.transitioned` 的 `providerId` 只有 A，完全看不出 B 也受影響）。這正是這支程式碼庫自己已知並在別處刻意迴避的坑：`mobile_sensors_stop`（mobile.rs:3197-3201）明寫「受器是全域開關，為了停一台而停用它，會讓另一台仍在串流的手機從 activeSensors 消失（＝感測靜默）」；`mobile_revoke`（mobile.rs:2614 起）因此刻意繞開 `Runtime::revoke_provider()`，改直接呼叫 `self.providers.transition()` 再搭配專屬的 `mobile_disable_high_risk_receptors`（2715）與 `mobile_stop_other_streaming_phones`（2868，會主動請其他仍在串流的手機停止並記 `mobile.sensors-stop-shared-receptor-off` 稽核）。但本分支新增、經由**通用**入口（CLI `providers transition`/`providers revoke`、HTTP `POST /v1/providers/{id}/transition`、`/revoke`）觸發的 `disable_provider_capabilities` 完全沒有這層防護，直接繞過所有 mobile 專屬安全機制去動同一份 registry 旗標。這違反「每個共享狀態只有一個 owner」與「感測不靜默」兩條不變量，且是本分支新引入（原本 `transition_provider(Disabled)` 對 mobile 幾乎是 no-op，見 v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md X2 列）、完全沒有測試涵蓋（`tests/mobile_loop.rs:4076` 唯一的通用撤銷測試 `generic_provider_revoke_stops_a_streaming_phone_and_drops_its_connection` 只配對一支手機）。同一支程式碼的另一半（`stop_provider_sensing`→`MobileSensorSource::release`，sensor_source.rs:415-448、mobile.rs:964-969）反而正確地用 target 把效果限定在單一裝置，證明這是修復時漏接的一個維度，不是刻意的設計取捨。
confirmed.evidence: providers.rs:1270-1272,1323-1358（新 `disable_provider_capabilities` 直接吃 desc.receptors/actuators 逐一 set_*_enabled(false)，無任何裝置族群/共用性檢查）；mobile.rs:188-206（MOBILE_RECEPTORS/MOBILE_ACTUATORS 為全域常數）；mobile.rs:3284-3292（mobile_register_provider：每台手機的 descriptor 塞入完全相同的共用陣列，註解明講「所有已配對 iPhone 共用」）；mobile.rs:3197-3201（mobile_sensors_stop 的既有註解，證明作者已知且刻意迴避同一風險）；mobile.rs:2614-2660、2715-2740、2868-2896（mobile_revoke 的專屬安全機制：直接動 self.providers、mobile_disable_high_risk_receptors、mobile_stop_other_streaming_phones + 專屬稽核 mobile.sensors-stop-shared-receptor-off，全部被通用路徑繞過）；crates/interaction-cli/src/main.rs:335-338（`providers transition`/`revoke` 為完全通用指令，無裝置種類守門）；crates/interaction-api/src/routes.rs:1329-1340（`POST /v1/providers/{id}/transition` 同樣無守門）；crates/interaction-runtime/tests/mobile_loop.rs:4076-4110（唯一涵蓋通用 revoke 對 mobile 效果的測試只配對一支手機，未觸及共用旗標的多手機場景）；本輪已知限制表格 docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md 的 X2 行自承「PATCH state=disabled 對 mobile 幾乎 no-op（不翻 receptor 旗標）」，證實這條路徑對 mobile 的實際旗標效果是本分支才新引入。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified end-to-end by reading the actual code, not just the finding's citations.

(1) MOBILE_RECEPTORS/MOBILE_ACTUATORS (mobile.rs:188-206) are literal string constants, and mobile_register_provider (mobile.rs:3284-3292) puts the exact same literal ids into every paired phone's ProviderDescriptor — confirmed by its own comment: "these six are not per-device; they're the set all paired iPhones share".

(2) CapabilityRegistry (interaction-registry/src/lib.rs:36-38) stores receptors/actuators in one process-wide BTreeMap keyed by that literal id — one entry for "iphone.mic-level", one for "iphone.haptic", etc., not one per device.

(3) disable_provider_capabilities (providers.rs:1323-1358), added on this branch and invoked unconditionally from transition_provider (1270-1272) for Disabled/Closed/Expired and from revoke_provider (1409-1447) for Revoked, iterates desc.receptors/desc.actuators and calls registry.set_receptor_enabled/set_actuator_enabled(false) with zero check on provider kind/origin/device-sharing — so disabling or revoking ANY one phone's provider id flips the single shared registry entries, which every other phone's dispatch path reads. Confirmed via registry.actuator()/receptor() (lib.rs:156-171,267-293), which key off the same single enabled flag, and via the existing with_two_phones_an_act_must_name_its_target_and_the_receipt_records_it test which proves "iphone.haptic" is genuinely one shared Actuator instance serving all paired phones by deviceId param, not one instance per phone.

(4) The mobile-specific paths (mobile_revoke at mobile.rs:2614-2660, mobile_sensors_stop, estop) deliberately bypass Runtime::revoke_provider()/transition_provider() and instead call self.providers.transition() directly plus mobile_disable_high_risk_receptors + mobile_stop_other_streaming_phones, exactly as the finding says, with comments explicitly documenting the shared-receptor hazard they're avoiding (mobile.rs:3197-3201, 2860-2867). Nothing in transition_provider/revoke_provider/disable_provider_capabilities calls into that compensating machinery, and the CLI (main.rs 335-345 -> commands.rs 1107-1122) and HTTP routes (routes.rs:1329-1340,1362) are fully generic with no device-kind gating anywhere in the chain — confirmed by grep.

(5) The only existing test for the generic revoke path (mobile_loop.rs:4076 generic_provider_revoke_stops_a_streaming_phone_and_drops_its_connection) pairs exactly one phone; there is no multi-phone test of transition_provider/revoke_provider anywhere.

(6) The audit written by disable_provider_capabilities (providers.rs:1345-1356) and by revoke_provider only names desc.identity.id (the single revoked/disabled device), even though the actuator/receptor flags it flips are shared — so the audit trail is misleading about blast radius, matching the finding's claim.

One partial mitigation I found that the finding did not mention: mobile.rs:2916-2954 has a pre-existing background watcher (mobile_spawn_receptor_off_watcher, built for a prior "safety-invariants-056" issue) that listens for the generic ReceptorOffline event on any high-risk receptor and calls mobile_stop_other_streaming_phones for any OTHER currently-streaming phone — and disable_provider_capabilities's registry.set_receptor_enabled(false) call does emit that same ReceptorOffline event (registry/lib.rs:162-171) without calling note_self_receptor_disable to suppress it. So for the receptor/mic-level slice specifically, other streaming phones will NOT silently vanish from activeSensors — they get pushed into an honest "stopping/result-unknown" state instead, i.e. the literal "sensor silencing" framing is softened by an existing safety net the finding didn't credit.

However this does not save the finding: (a) it still means revoking/disabling one phone force-stops another phone's actively-streaming, uninvolved microphone as an undocumented, unaudited (from that other device's perspective) side effect — a real single-owner/shared-state violation on its own; and (b) there is no equivalent watcher or compensation whatsoever for ActuatorOffline (registry/lib.rs:260,280) — so iphone.haptic, iphone.notify, iphone.tts, iphone.torch, iphone.flash, and iphone.character (the character-presentation actuator) go silently and permanently disabled for every paired phone, with no notice to their owners and no audit naming them, purely as a side effect of revoking or disabling a single (possibly unrelated or lost) phone's provider.

This is a genuine, newly-introduced (this branch's disable_provider_capabilities), completely untested cross-device capability leak that violates the "each shared state has exactly one owner" invariant and meaningfully degrades safety/availability for uninvolved devices without any audit trail pointing at them. I keep the severity at the top of this schema's scale ("blocker", mapping to the finding's original "critical"): it is a cross-tenant blast-radius bug in a security-relevant lifecycle operation (revoke/disable), it is silent from the affected devices' point of view for actuators, the audit is misleading, and it has zero test coverage despite this exact family of hazard being called out and carefully engineered around elsewhere in the same file for the mobile-specific entry points.

Verified end-to-end against the current file contents (no line drift).

1. `crates/interaction-registry/src/lib.rs:113-169` — `receptors`/`actuators` are a `BTreeMap<Id, Entry>` keyed only by the literal capability-id string, with a single global `enabled: bool` per id. There is no per-provider or per-device dimension to this flag.

2. `crates/interaction-runtime/src/mobile.rs:2451-2506` (`mobile_register_capabilities`) registers exactly one `PushReceptor`/`MobileActuator` instance per literal id (`iphone.motion`, `iphone.battery`, `iphone.touch`, `iphone.mic-level`, `iphone.haptic`, `iphone.notify`, `iphone.tts`, `iphone.torch`, `iphone.flash`, `iphone.character`) — called once from `mobile_ensure_started`, not per paired device. `mobile_register_provider` (mobile.rs:3273-3292) then gives *every* paired phone's `ProviderDescriptor` the identical literal arrays `MOBILE_RECEPTORS`/`MOBILE_ACTUATORS`, with an explicit comment confirming these are shared, not per-device.

3. `disable_provider_capabilities` (providers.rs:1323-1358, new this branch) takes exactly that shared descriptor and does `set_receptor_enabled(id, false)` / `set_actuator_enabled(id, false)` per literal id — with no check for whether another provider (another paired phone) also depends on the same id. It is invoked unconditionally from `transition_provider` (providers.rs:1270) whenever `provider_stopped(state)` is true, i.e. for `Disabled | Closed | Expired | Revoked` (confirmed via `interaction-registry/src/providers.rs:23-30`). `revoke_provider` (providers.rs:1409-1423) has the same unscoped loop, pre-existing from before this branch (verified via `git show 8f52837:...providers.rs`).

4. The mobile-specific protections the finding cites are real and do exist, but are bypassed by both generic paths: `mobile_revoke` (mobile.rs:2614) calls `self.providers.transition()` directly (not `Runtime::transition_provider`), then `mobile_disable_high_risk_receptors` and `mobile_stop_other_streaming_phones` (which sends `stop-all` to every *other* connected phone and logs `mobile.sensors-stop-shared-receptor-off`, per the passing test `one_phone_disconnecting_never_silently_hides_another_streaming_phone`, mobile_loop.rs:3346). Neither `transition_provider` nor `revoke_provider` (the generic, CLI/HTTP-reachable functions — cli/main.rs `ProvidersAction::Transition`/`Revoke`, routes.rs `provider_transition`/`provider_revoke`) call any of that machinery; they only call the newly-added, per-device-scoped `stop_provider_sensing`→`MobileSensorSource::release(target=this device)` (correctly scoped) *after* already having flipped the shared flag (not scoped at all).

5. `docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md:85` (row X2) confirms the pre-branch state: `PATCH state=disabled` was "幾乎 no-op（不翻 receptor 旗標）" for mobile. This branch's fix is exactly what wires `disable_provider_capabilities` into `transition_provider`'s Disabled/Closed/Expired arm — so while the Revoked-state version of this bug already existed via `revoke_provider` before this branch, the branch newly extends the same unscoped, cross-device-affecting behavior to three more states reachable through the fully generic transition endpoint, without adding the multi-phone mitigation. That is an in-scope regression, not merely pre-existing code left untouched.

6. Test coverage gap is real: `generic_provider_revoke_stops_a_streaming_phone_and_drops_its_connection` (mobile_loop.rs:4078) pairs one phone and asserts the shared `iphone.mic-level` receptor ends up globally `Err` (disabled) — exactly the mechanism the finding describes — but with only one phone paired, so it can't catch the cross-device blast radius. The only test with two concurrently-streaming phones (`one_phone_disconnecting_never_silently_hides_another_streaming_phone`) exercises the *disconnect* path (which does go through `mobile_stop_other_streaming_phones` and is properly mitigated), not the generic transition/revoke path. So there is genuinely no test proving device B survives an admin `disable`/`revoke` issued against device A.

I downgrade "critical"→"high" rather than refuting: this is a real, verified violation of the "感測不靜默" and "single owner per shared state" invariants with concrete, silent, cross-device impact (an admin disabling one lost/misbehaving phone can silently kill haptic/notify/tts/torch/flash/character — and the still-consent-gated mic — for every other paired phone, unaudited beyond the acted-on provider's id). I hold back from "blocker" only because: it requires deliberate admin action on a specific device (not a spontaneous safety/estop bypass), needs >1 phone concurrently paired (a real but not universal deployment shape), and most of the collaterally-disabled actuators (non-consent-required: haptic/notify/tts/torch/flash/character) self-heal on the next daemon restart because `register_receptor`/`register_actuator` re-derive `enabled` from manifest defaults (`registry/lib.rs:113-127`) rather than from persisted state — only the consent-gated mic-level stays off, which is otherwise the intended "high-risk doesn't auto-recover" behavior, just misapplied to an uninvolved device.

confirmed.fix: `disable_provider_capabilities` 在處理 receptors/actuators 之前，先問一句「這個能力 id 是否還被其他 operational provider 宣告/使用」（可用 `ProviderRegistry` 反查所有仍在 Available/Busy 等操作中狀態、且 receptors/actuators 包含同一 id 的其他 provider）；若有，代表這是家族共用能力，通用路徑不得直接關閉旗標，而應改走該家族自己的協調器（mobile 已有 `mobile_disable_high_risk_receptors`＋`mobile_stop_other_streaming_phones`）或至少對其餘持有者送出等效的停止請求並記錄專屬稽核，避免無聲波及；同時 `provider.capabilities-disabled`／`provider.transitioned` 稽核應誠實列出「這個旗標其實也影響哪些其他 provider」，不能只寫被操作的那一個 id。
confirmed.regressionTest:
In crates/interaction-runtime/tests/mobile_loop.rs: pair two phones A and B via pair(&rt) twice. Enable the iphone.mic-level receptor and iphone.haptic actuator, have B send a status message with micLevel=true and wait_for_iphone_mic_sensor(&rt,true) so B is an active mic stream; also grab an enabled_actuator(&rt,'iphone.haptic') handle and confirm it can target B via deviceId. Then call the GENERIC path on A only: rt.revoke_provider(&mobile_provider_id(&id_a)) (or rt.transition_provider(&mobile_provider_id(&id_a), ProviderState::Disabled)). Assert: (1) rt.registry.actuator(&ActuatorId::new('iphone.haptic')) now returns Err even though B was never touched, i.e. an actuator.execute() targeted at deviceId=B now fails with "actuator iphone.haptic is disabled"; (2) same for iphone.notify/iphone.character; (3) the provider.revoked/provider.capabilities-disabled audit only names id_a, not id_b, even though B's actuators are now unusable; (4) (secondary, to characterize rather than assume) observe whether B's mic stream gets force-stopped via the receptor-off watcher — it will, proving that revoking A involuntarily terminates B's independent, unrelated sensing session as an unaudited-from-B's-perspective side effect. / In crates/interaction-runtime/tests/mobile_loop.rs, add a test modeled on `generic_provider_revoke_stops_a_streaming_phone_and_drops_its_connection` but with two paired phones:
1. `pair(&rt)` twice → (id_a, ws_a), (id_b, ws_b).
2. Enable `iphone.mic-level`, send phone-status(recording=true) from both, wait until `status().activeSensors` shows both.
3. Call `rt.transition_provider(&mobile_provider_id(&id_a), ProviderState::Disabled)` (or `rt.revoke_provider(&pid_a)`).
4. Assert (currently fails): `rt.registry.receptor(&ReceptorId::new("iphone.mic-level")).await` is `Ok` (B's mic capability must remain enabled) — today it is `Err` because the shared flag was flipped.
5. Assert ws_b receives no unsolicited `stop-all` (today none is sent — B just silently loses the capability with no notice) and `status().activeSensors` for B never enters "unknown consequence" limbo the way the disconnect path handles it — today B is neither notified nor reflected honestly, it just silently can't have new observations accepted.
6. Assert no audit entry names device B, while `iphone.haptic`/`iphone.notify`/etc. registered under B's descriptor are also confirmed still enabled after the assertion in step 4 generalized to the other ids.

confirmed.title: resume 的 patches[] 混雜「本地已透過其他管道追上」的舊項時，其後真正新的補丁會被靜默丟棄且不觸發 realign
confirmed.file: apps/interaction-desktop/src/aip/sessionClient.ts:442-445,466-470
confirmed.claim: `ingestResume()` 的 patches 迴圈把「這一項沒有把本地精確推進到它自己的 revision」一律當成『序列中斷、必須停下』處理（`const applied = current.local?.revision === message.revision; if (!applied) break;`，第 469-470 行）。但『沒有精確命中』有兩種完全不同的情況：(a) 真正的缺口（`alignState` 已經回 `realign`，此時 `outcome.effects.length > 0` 會在第 468 行提前 return，帶著 realign effect，這條路徑是對的）；(b) 這一項其實是『**已經**透過另一條管道（非這次 resume 的訊息鏈）追過了』的良性 stale/duplicate 情況——此時 `outcome.effects` 是空的，於是流程直接落到第 469-470 行的 `break`，**不帶任何 effect** 就中止迴圈，把陣列裡排在它後面、revision 確實比本地新的補丁全部丟棄，也不會設定 `counters.realign` 或觸發 `setRealign`。呼叫端（`CharacterSyncCard.tsx`）完全看不到任何訊號要再對齊一次。
confirmed.evidence:
1) 用真實模組跑出的反例（非假設）：先以一則 SSE snapshot 把本地對齊到 revision=5；再 `fetch-issued`（模擬呼叫端已發出 resume，帶著 lastRevision=5）；接著模擬本地『透過另一個管道』被推進到 revision=50（用一則不同 messageId 的 SSE snapshot，模擬下方第 2 點列出的真實觸發路徑）；最後餵入 `resume-response`，其 `patches[]` 是 host 依『client 送出時記得的 lastRevision=5』回放的 6..60 全段補丁（每項都是全新、不曾在本地 `seen` 環出現過的 messageId）。結果：`after.local.revision === 50`（卡住，revision 51-60 全部消失）、`effects` 為空陣列——沒有任何 realign 或 unrecoverable 訊號。（測試檔已放在 scratchpad，`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-user-Workspace-claude-lab-adaptive-interaction/0e6be2eb-b2e4-418e-90f7-06f7a1b7a6c5/scratchpad/resume-gap2.test.ts`，用 vitest 對照真正的 `src/aip/sessionClient.ts` 執行，非猜測。）
2) 這個『本地透過另一條管道被推進』的前提在目前 Runtime 是真實可觸發的，不是純理論：`crates/interaction-session/src/session.rs` 的 `handle_capability()`（約行 1320-1332）在既有成員重新協商時（`join()` 走既有成員分支，即『重新協商是存活證明』的心跳路徑），會把 `joined.snapshot_envelope`（`reason: None`、`sessionEpoch=self.epoch`、`revision=self.revision` 的**完整快照**，訊息 id 是 `next_message_id()` 全新產生的，與任何補丁 log entry 的 id 都不同）包成 `Output::Send { to: bound_identity, envelope: snapshot_envelope }`。`crates/interaction-runtime/src/character_session.rs` 的 `character_session_send()`（約行 1856-1858）對『非 `PartyKind::Device`』的對象（`PartyKind::Renderer`——外部角色 adapter；`PartyKind::HumanSurface`——桌面本身）一律落到 `_ => self.publish_character_session_state(envelope)`（約行 1862-1868），這是**沒有對象區分的全域 SSE bus**（`self.events.publish(RuntimeEvent::new(EventType::CharacterSessionState, ...))`），桌面 `CharacterSyncCard.tsx` 正是透過同一個 `character.session.state` 事件把資料餵進 `dispatch({kind:'sse', envelope})`（`interaction-api/src/sse.rs` 行 51/177 對應同一 `EventType::CharacterSessionState`）。也就是說：**只要有另一個 Renderer 身分的角色 adapter（或任何非 Device 成員）在桌面正在跑一次 `resume`（例如 `connectionKey` 因 SSE 重連而 +1 觸發）的同一時間重新協商（它自己的重連心跳），桌面就會經 SSE 收到一份完整 snapshot，把本地推進到當下的 revision；隨後那個仍在飛行中、依『舊 lastRevision』請求的 resume 一旦回來，其 `patches[]` 就會呈現本文重現的『前段已被追過、後段仍是全新』的形狀。**
3) 對照既有測試：`src/test/session-client.test.ts` 只涵蓋『patches 連續套用成功』『中間一則 baseRevision 接不上就 realign』『空 patches』三種情形（行 458-521），完全沒有涵蓋『patches 陣列前段是 stale/duplicate、後段仍是全新』這一種——這正是本檔案自己在開頭宣稱『所有協定判斷都在這裡』『不硬套、不猜』所要防的那類問題，卻恰好是測試沒蓋到的洞。

verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed by direct code reading and by running a reproduction against the real (unmocked) src/aip/sessionClient.ts via vitest.

Mechanism, verified line-by-line against the current file:
- `ingestMessage` (lines 433-448) has a shortcut at 442-445: when `authoritative && machine.appliedSinceIssue && notNewerThanLocal(local, message)` it returns `{ next: {...bump 'stale'}, effects: [] }` WITHOUT ever calling `alignState`. This is a valid, benign "already caught up elsewhere" outcome.
- `ingestResume`'s patches loop (451-476) treats "no effects" as proof the item advanced local to exactly `message.revision` (line 469: `const applied = current.local?.revision === message.revision`). That equivalence is false for the stale/duplicate branch above: local can be far ahead of `message.revision`, so `applied` is `false` and the loop `break`s at line 470 — silently, with zero effects — abandoning every later (genuinely newer) item in `patches[]`.

Reproduction (ran with real module, not mocked, via `pnpm vitest run`):
1. Align to revision=5 via SSE snapshot.
2. `fetch-issued` (simulating a resume request remembering lastRevision=5).
3. While that "request" is in flight, another SSE snapshot (distinct messageId) advances local to revision=50 — setting `appliedSinceIssue=true` (this models a concurrent channel, verified as realistically reachable below).
4. Feed `resume-response` with `patches[]` covering revision 6..60, each a genuinely new messageId/hash chained off the previous state.

Read the actual code end-to-end and confirmed every load-bearing claim.

1. declarative_session.rs is a brand-new file on this branch (git log shows it introduced whole in commit 600f030, part of this branch's diff vs base 8f52837), so it is squarely in scope.

The match on `channel.stop_all()`'s result maps `Unavailable→Unreachable`, `Refused→Refused`, any other Err→`Unknown`, and in none of these branches is the receptor flag ever restored to `true`. I grepped the whole file for `set_receptor_enabled` and it is called exactly once, always with `false` — confirming the flip is never reverted programmatically.

4. I traced registry semantics: `interaction-registry/src/lib.rs` `receptor()` returns `Err(Unavailable)` iff `entry.enabled == false`, and `set_receptor_enabled` is the only thing that flips that bit.    - `active_captures()` (declarative_session.rs:458-484) computes its result purely from `self.enabled_high_risk(&rt)` (line 424-428), which is a synchronous read of the registry's `receptor_enabled` flag. There is no independent "stopping/stop-unknown" state tracked anywhere in `DeclarativeSensorSource`.

   - `tests/sensors_loop.rs:563-573` `FakeSensorSource::active_captures` likewise only clears `capturing` on a `Confirm` outcome and reports `SENSOR_STATE_STOP_UNKNOWN` while `stop_requested` is true and `capturing` is still true for Timeout/Unreachable/Refuse — the same correct pattern.

Verified end-to-end by reading the current file, not just the quoted snippets.

1) `foregroundDidResume()` (SessionClient.swift:533-548) and its lifecycle wiring (AppLifecycle.swift's `LifecycleDecision.on`, ConnectionManager.swift `lifecyclePhaseChanged` L480-529, and the ScenePhase hookup in InteractionCompanionApp.swift) are entirely NEW in this branch (`git diff 8f52837..HEAD` shows AppLifecycle.swift as a wholly new 139-line file, and `foregroundDidResume` as a new function in the SessionClient.swift diff). True for every `sendResume` call site, but only `foregroundDidResume` can fire repeatedly with zero real desync evidence.
4) `noteResumeAttempt` genuinely counts at *send* time, not at failure/timeout time — the doc-comment says so explicitly ("送出一次 resume 就記一次「還沒對齊」"), and this is a pre-existing, deliberately tested design choice: `SessionClientTests.swift`'s `testEveryCountedResumeAttemptIsActuallySentAndReconnectingRestoresTheBudget` explicitly pins "counting happens before the response arrives" as intentional ("使用者看到「無法恢復」時實際只做過 2 次 round-trip"). So three real `.active` transitions (each requiring `sinceForeground >= 1s`, per `LifecycleDecision.on`) landing before any host reply arrives would indeed drive `resumeFailures` to 3 purely from send-count, not from confirmed failures — confirmed by comparing to the analogous desktop reducer (`apps/interaction-desktop/src/aip/sessionClient.ts`), which only bumps its equivalent `realignStreak` when a *received* message signals actual mismatch (epoch/base/hash), never merely on sending a request. `LifecycleTests.swift` and `SessionClientTests.swift` never call `foregroundDidResume()` more than once without an intervening host reply, so this path is genuinely untested. Mitigating factors that argue the severity is overstated: (1) the scenario needs two coincident rare conditions — three genuine ≥1s background/foreground cycles *and* a host slow enough that none of the three resume round-trips complete in that window (LAN WebSocket RTT is normally tens of ms; the host's resume handler in `character_session.rs` replies synchronously per frame with no queuing that would stall it under normal conditions); (2) the resulting `unrecoverable` state is not sticky — `handleResponse` (713-) and `consume`'s `.applied` case (755-756) call `SessionDecisions.noteSyncSucceeded(&local)` unconditionally, i.e. NOT gated on `local.unrecoverable`, so as soon as any one of the outstanding resume replies arrives (even after the false "unrecoverable" was set), the counter and flag reset back to healthy — the false claim is very likely to self-correct within one round trip rather than persist; (3) the feature is explicitly simulator-only verified (README/CHANGELOG: "模擬器 XCTest 120/120，真機零執行"), consistent with the project's own stated honesty practice about undemonstrated real-device paths, so labeling a narrow, self-healing race in an unverified-on-hardware feature as "high" overstates its practical impact relative to a durable/irreversible false claim.

Swift's `SessionClient.apply` (SessionClient.swift:293-313) mirrors Rust exactly: when `!reset`, only revision is checked, and the message is applied with `epoch: message.epoch` (silently overwriting local epoch) regardless of whether it changed. So for the same snapshot message (epoch differs, no session-reset reason, revision > local revision), TS produces `realign` while Rust/Swift both apply and adopt the new epoch — a genuine third divergence. The file's own "兩處刻意差異" list (lines ~296-301) names only two patch-branch differences and omits this snapshot-branch one, so the self-description is factually incomplete — confirmed by reading that block directly. The regression test at session-client.test.ts:329-338 ("epoch 不同但沒有 reason → 不猜，回 realign") proves this is deliberate code, not an accident, which is exactly why it needed to be disclosed and wasn't.

I did try to refute evidence #2's specific reachability story (another member's `handle_capability` renegotiation snapshot leaking onto the desktop's SSE bus). Tracing `character_session_send` (character_session.rs:1824-1826) shows `Device`-kind targets go through `device_outbound`, never through `publish_character_session_state`; only non-Device targets (in practice, only the singleton desktop `HumanSurface` party, since `Party::device`/`Party::human_surface` are the only constructors used in production code) reach the SSE bus that way. So a *device's own* renegotiation cannot leak onto the desktop's stream as literally described. However this doesn't refute the finding: a simpler, equally reachable path exists — the desktop's own reconnect flow (§7 steps 1-2, `capability` sent before `resume`) drives `handle_capability` with `bound_identity = desktop_party()`, whose snapshot is always `reason: None` and does publish to the SSE bus; if any other device bumped `self.epoch` earlier via its own `resume()` (session.rs:795, which only tells the resuming party via a forced `session-reset` reason and nobody else), the desktop's stale local epoch will hit exactly this condition on its next reconnect. So the divergence is real and reachable, just via a slightly different exact wire path than evidence #2 describes; the core, title-level claim stands and is verified by direct code and test inspection, not inference.

confirmed.fix: 至少先把這第三處差異誠實補進檔案開頭與 `alignState` 附近的註解（讓『與 Rust 的差異』清單完整、不誤導）；再視 AIP 契約補一則跨語言 conformance fixture／文件小節，明確裁決『snapshot 的 epoch 不同但沒有 session-reset』時三端（Rust／TS／Swift）應該得到哪一種結論（目前是 Rust／Swift 直接接受＋改寫本地 epoch、只有 TS 選擇 realign），並讓三份實作真正一致，而不是各自解讀。

confirmed.title: Migration-save failure reuses the "backup could not be made" diagnostic text even when the backup succeeded
confirmed.file: crates/interaction-runtime/src/character_session.rs:669 (the `Ok(_) => match store.save(&session.snapshot())` arm; finding cited :668, off by one line but same statement)
confirmed.claim: In `CharacterSessionHost::open`'s `Startup::Migrate` branch, the `Ok(_) => match store.save(&session.snapshot()) { Ok(SaveOutcome::Written) => true, outcome => { ...; false } }` arm treats every non-`Written` outcome (`Ok(SkippedStale)`, `Ok(SkippedParked)`, and any `Err(PortError)` from the actual write/rename) identically to a failed backup: `landed` becomes `false` and `migration` is set to `(from, STORE_NOTE_MIGRATION_DEFERRED)`. But `STORE_NOTE_MIGRATION_DEFERRED`'s literal text is "…it was kept as it is because a backup could not be made" (character_session.rs:66-68). That text is only true for the sibling `Err(error)` arm on `std::fs::copy` (line 662-667), which explicitly calls `store.park(STORE_NOTE_MIGRATION_DEFERRED)`. When the backup copy *succeeds* but the subsequent `store.save()` fails for an unrelated reason (a transient rename/EIO/permission failure on the live file, disk-full between the two syscalls, a concurrent holder of the destination on some filesystems), the diagnostics will falsely claim the backup failed, and — unlike the true backup-failure path — the store is *not* parked in this sub-case (no `store.park(...)` call in the `outcome` arm), so a later successful periodic persist will silently rewrite the file to the current format without ever updating `host.migration()`/`load_note` (both are computed once at `open()` and never revisited). The end state exposed via `character_session_diagnostics_value()`'s `store` object can then show `format: 1` (already migrated) together with a stale `migratedFrom: 0` / `migrationNote` that says the backup could not be made — an internally inconsistent, honesty-ladder-violating diagnostic for a real (if narrow) failure window.

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified against the current file, not just the pasted evidence.

1. The whole `Startup::Migrate` mechanism (`SaveOutcome`, `JsonSessionStore::park`, `StoreStatus`, `CharacterSessionHost::migration()`) is new in this branch (git diff 8f52837..HEAD shows it added wholesale), so this is squarely an in-scope finding, not pre-existing code.

2. The exact code quoted in the finding is present verbatim today (crates/interaction-runtime/src/character_session.rs:663-679, the `Ok(_) => match store.save(&session.snapshot())` arm at line 669): the wildcard `outcome => { ...; false }` arm catches *every* non-`Written` result — `Ok(SkippedStale)`, `Ok(SkippedParked)`, and any `Err(PortError)` — and, unlike the sibling `Err(error)` (copy-failed) arm just above it, never calls `store.park(...)`.

3. I checked whether `SkippedStale`/`SkippedParked` are actually reachable at this call site: `CharacterSession::restore_report` bumps the restored revision by `config.persist_every_revisions` (session.rs:349, default/clamped to ≥1), so the snapshot passed to `store.save` here always has `(epoch, revision)` strictly greater than what `seed_from` committed during the preceding `store.load()`, and `state.parked` cannot have been set between `load()` and this `save()` (single-threaded startup, and `load()`'s own success path never parks). So the one *realistic* trigger for the wildcard arm is `Err(PortError)` from `write_owner_only`'s rename/write step (JsonSessionStore::save, character_session.rs ~485-503) — e.g. a transient rename/EIO/permission failure or disk-full between the successful backup copy and the save. That exactly matches the finding's core scenario.

4. In that scenario: `migration` is set to `(from, STORE_NOTE_MIGRATION_DEFERRED)` — text that literally reads "...because a backup could not be made" (character_session.rs:66-68) — even though the backup *did* succeed and the real cause was the save/write failing. The store is left un-parked, so any later successful persist (e.g. `character_session_persist`, called from ordinary `Output::Persist` handling, line ~1871) will write `session.snapshot()`, whose `format` field is always the crate's current `SNAPSHOT_FORMAT` (session.rs:761) — updating `store.status().format` to the new format — while `host.migration()` is a struct field computed once in `open()` and never revisited (confirmed by its own doc comment: "只進新的 store 欄位"). `character_session_diagnostics_value()` (character_session.rs:924-972) surfaces both `store.format` and `migratedFrom`/`migrationNote` side by side, so the window described (new `format` alongside a stale, wrongly-worded `migrationNote`) is real and reachable, not merely theoretical.

5. Confirmed no existing test covers this: the only two migration-failure tests (`an_older_format_file_is_migrated_and_the_original_is_backed_up`, `a_migration_that_cannot_back_up_leaves_the_original_alone`) both exercise the *backup-copy* failure (`Err(error)` arm, via occupying the backup path with a directory) — I ran the first to confirm current passing behavior and inspected both; neither exercises "copy succeeds, then `store.save` fails."

This is a genuine honesty-ladder violation (CLAUDE.md's 誠實階梯 / 感測不靜默 spirit extended to persistence diagnostics): a real, if narrow, failure window produces a diagnostic that misattributes the cause and can silently become internally inconsistent after self-healing. Medium severity is appropriate — no data loss or safety-invariant breach (the live file is never corrupted or wrongly overwritten with bad content), but a boot-time+ongoing diagnostic can be actively wrong about why persistence was deferred.

confirmed.fix: Give the write-after-backup failure its own fixed-text constant (e.g. `STORE_NOTE_MIGRATION_WRITE_FAILED`, "the migrated snapshot could not be written; the original format is still on disk") instead of reusing `STORE_NOTE_MIGRATION_DEFERRED`, and decide deliberately whether that sub-case should also `store.park(...)` (consistent with the port's own invariant #2: "只跳過開機那一次不夠——之後每一次 persist 都會 rename 蓋掉它") or is intentionally left retryable — either way the diagnostic text must match what actually happened. Add a test that seeds a readable old-format file, lets the backup copy succeed, and forces the live-path write to fail (e.g. via a read-only parent directory scoped just around the `store.save` call, or a small test seam) to pin the expected note/parked state.
confirmed.regressionTest:
Add a test alongside `a_migration_that_cannot_back_up_leaves_the_original_alone` that lets the backup *succeed* but forces the subsequent `store.save` to fail, then re-opens and checks the diagnostics stay internally consistent over time:
1. Seed `state_dir/character-session.json` with `legacy_format0_body()` (format 0) as in the existing tests, but do NOT occupy the `.pre-format-0` backup path (so `std::fs::copy` succeeds).
2. Force the *live-file* rename in `write_owner_only` to fail on the first attempt only — e.g. spawn a watcher thread that polls for the backup file's appearance and immediately `chmod`s the state directory to remove write permission (0o500) right after the backup lands but before `open()`'s subsequent `store.save(&session.snapshot())` call reaches its rename; restore write permission after that one call (best-effort/racy, may need a short retry loop to hit the window reliably — or, better, add a `#[cfg(test)]` fault-injection hook such as a thread-local `AtomicBool` checked at the top of `write_owner_only` that forces one `Err(PortError::Unavailable)`, flipped off after first use).
3. Assert after `open()`: `host.migration() == Some((0, STORE_NOTE_MIGRATION_DEFERRED))`, `host.store().status().parked == false` (unlike the copy-failure case), and `host.store().status().last_persist_error == Some(PERSIST_ERROR_WRITE)` — proving the store is writable again despite the misleading "backup could not be made" note.
4. Clear the fault, then drive one successful persist (e.g. call `host.store().save(&host.session().snapshot())` directly, mirroring test `an_older_format_file_is_migrated_and_the_original_is_backed_up`'s pattern) and assert it returns `Ok(SaveOutcome::Written)` and `host.store().status().format == Some(interaction_session::SNAPSHOT_FORMAT)`, while `host.migration()` is still `Some((0, STORE_NOTE_MIGRATION_DEFERRED))` — demonstrating the inconsistent `{format: <current>, migrationNote: "...backup could not be made"}` diagnostic snapshot that `character_session_diagnostics_value()` would expose.

confirmed.title: Party 缺 deny_unknown_fields：members[].party 夾帶的未知鍵繞過 restore 的「未知欄位一律拒絕」
confirmed.file: crates/interaction-aip/src/message.rs:94 (Party struct, missing deny_unknown_fields); crates/interaction-session/src/state.rs:235 (MemberView.party uses bare Party, not the party_ref string wrapper); reachable via crates/interaction-session/src/session.rs:330-364 (restore_report) and crates/interaction-runtime/src/character_session.rs:579 (CharacterSessionHost::open); existing test crates/interaction-session/tests/session_hardening.rs:717-759 (session-integrity-061) claims "nested pollution is blocked the same way" but never tests inside party.
confirmed.claim: M1 §2.2/§2.3（commit e34ab17）把 CharacterSession::restore 原本的第二次 canonical-hash 覆核（`if state_hash(&canonical) != snapshot.hash { return Err(HashMismatch) }`）拿掉，改宣稱『未知鍵改由 deny_unknown_fields＋attention 允許鍵檢查擋住』——CHANGELOG.md「快照檔格式版本與遷移」段與 crates/interaction-session/src/session.rs:288-293 的清單明列 SemanticState／Mood／TruthView／LastInteraction／MemberView 都是 deny_unknown_fields，attention 另外用 attention_keys_are_known（session.rs:198-208, 333）補洞。但這份清單漏了 MemberView.party 的巢狀型別 Party（crates/interaction-aip/src/message.rs:92-97，只有 `#[serde(rename_all="camelCase")]`，沒有 deny_unknown_fields）。deny_unknown_fields 不會遞迴進巢狀型別，所以 members[].party 物件裡多塞一個鍵時，Party 的 Deserialize 會靜默丟掉它，不會回 InvalidState；而移除後的 restore 不再要求『反序列化後重序列化＝原文』，只把差異記成 RestoreReport.canonical_changed（migration 訊號，不是拒絕）。結果是：一份把 members[0].party 塞了未知鍵、且重新算過自洽 hash 的 snapshot，會被 CharacterSession::restore/restore_report 直接接受並成為權威狀態——正是 session.rs:288-291 那段註解明白說要防的『被污染的 state 若原樣還原，會被當成權威狀態重新廣播給所有成員』。這條路徑就是 daemon 真實開機路徑：crates/interaction-runtime/src/character_session.rs:579 的 CharacterSessionHost::open 直接呼叫 restore_report，needs_migration()==true 時走 Startup::Migrate（續接＋事後才備份原檔＋以新格式落地），並未在讀入當下拒絕。
confirmed.evidence: 用與 repo 相同版本的三個 crate（interaction-aip/interaction-session/interaction-character，path 依賴）在 scratchpad 寫了一支獨立小程式重現：用 CharacterSession::join 產生一份合法 session，序列化成 state，手動在 members[0].party 塞入 `"evilKey":"smuggled"`，用同一支 state_hash() 對整份（含 evilKey 的）state 重算 hash 做成一份『自洽』的 Snapshot，餵給 CharacterSession::restore_report(config, &snapshot, now)。實際輸出：`ACCEPTED despite smuggled key in members[].party.evilKey` / `format_from=1 canonical_changed=true` / `restored members[0].party = {"id":"desktop","kind":"human-surface"}`（evilKey 被靜默丟掉，不是被拒絕）。對照分支前（base commit 8f52837）的 crates/interaction-session/src/session.rs::restore：同一份 tampered snapshot 會因為 `state_hash(&canonical)`（canonical 不含 evilKey）對不上 `snapshot.hash`（對含 evilKey 的原文算的）而回 SessionError::HashMismatch——確認這是本分支新引入的回歸，不是既有行為。cargo test -p interaction-session --test state_hash_fixtures 與 -p interaction-aip --test conformance 目前全綠，因為現有 9 個 state-hash fixtures／state_semantics.rs 都沒有『members[].party 帶未知鍵』這個情境。

verdicts.reasoning:
Fully verified by independent reproduction. `Party` (interaction-aip/src/message.rs:94-97) has no `deny_unknown_fields`; `MemberView.party` (interaction-session/src/state.rs:235) uses this bare `Party` type directly (not the string-wrapped `party_ref` used elsewhere for `Attention::Member`/`LastInteraction.source`), so `deny_unknown_fields` on `MemberView`/`SemanticState` does not reject unknown keys nested inside the `party` sub-object — standard serde non-recursion behavior, correctly diagnosed.

Built an out-of-tree crate that path-depends on the real interaction-aip/interaction-session/interaction-character crates (no repo files touched), joined a device member into a fresh CharacterSession, took a legitimate snapshot, injected `"evilKey":"smuggled"` into `members[0].party`, recomputed `snapshot.hash` via the same `interaction_aip::canonical_hash` the implementation uses, and called `CharacterSession::restore_report`. Result: ACCEPTED (format_from=1, canonical_changed=true), restored party silently dropped evilKey rather than the snapshot being rejected.

Confirmed regression vs base: `git show 8f52837:.../session.rs` shows the pre-M1 `restore` had a second `state_hash(&canonical) != snapshot.hash` check right after computing canonical, which would have caught exactly this tampering (canonical lacks evilKey so its hash differs from the attacker-forged hash over the tampered original). M1 removed that check, replacing the canonical/original diff with `RestoreReport.canonical_changed`, a non-rejecting migration signal only.

Confirmed real boot path: `CharacterSessionHost::open` (interaction-runtime/src/character_session.rs:579) calls `restore_report` directly; `needs_migration()==true` (true here) routes to `Startup::Migrate`, which backs up the original and persists the canonical snapshot without rejecting at load — exactly as claimed.

Found the directly relevant existing test `restore_rejects_a_poisoned_snapshot_even_with_a_matching_hash` (session-integrity-061, session_hardening.rs:717-759): its docstring says "巢狀污染（成員投影裡）一樣擋掉" (nested pollution is blocked the same way), but its "nested" case only inserts the evil key as a *sibling* of `party` inside the member object — which MemberView's own deny_unknown_fields does catch — never inside `member["party"]` itself, so it never exercises the actual gap. Ran it (`cargo test -p interaction-session --test session_hardening restore_rejects_a_poisoned_snapshot_even_with_a_matching_hash`): passes, but for a different, already-guarded shape, so this doesn't contradict the finding. Also ran `-p interaction-session --test state_hash_fixtures` and `-p interaction-aip --test conformance`: both pass, confirming neither suite covers an unknown key nested inside `party`. All cited line numbers match the current files exactly — no drift.

Severity correction (high→medium): the actual authoritative state that gets persisted/broadcast is always the re-serialized `canonical` value, which never contains the smuggled key — it's dropped at deserialization, never incorporated or leaked downstream, so no attacker-controlled data actually reaches the broadcast state via this path. Separately, `canonical_hash` is a plain deterministic SHA-256 with no secret key, so anyone able to write the snapshot file could already forge any fully-valid, non-polluted `SemanticState` with a self-consistent hash regardless of this bug — the code's own comment concedes hash self-consistency was never an anti-forgery mechanism. So the marginal capability this specific gap grants an attacker is essentially nil. What's genuinely wrong: a documented, tested invariant ("多一個鍵就 InvalidState", "巢狀污染...一樣擋掉") has a real hole for `MemberView.party`, the existing test overstates its own coverage, and a tampered/corrupted snapshot that should be rejected/quarantined is instead silently normalized and accepted — a real defect worth fixing, but not a high-impact exploit given the inert consequence.

Reproduced end-to-end against the current tree (not against a stale/base version). Built an isolated crate that path-depends on the repo's real interaction-aip/interaction-session/interaction-character crates (same versions), used CharacterSession::join to get a legitimate snapshot, injected `"evilKey":"smuggled"` into `members[0].party`, recomputed a self-consistent hash with the real `state_hash()`, and called `CharacterSession::restore_report`. Result: `ACCEPTED ... format_from=1 canonical_changed=true`, exactly matching the finding's claimed output shape.

Confirmed facts:
- `Party` (crates/interaction-aip/src/message.rs:94) has `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` only, no `deny_unknown_fields`.
- `MemberView.party` (crates/interaction-session/src/state.rs:235) is typed as `Party` directly (not via the `party_ref` string-wrapper used for `Attention::Member.party` / `LastInteraction.source`), so it round-trips as a nested JSON object `{"kind":..,"id":..}` — and `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on `MemberView` (state.rs:233) does not recurse into that nested object's own Deserialize impl. This is standard serde behavior, correctly identified.
- git diff 8f52837..HEAD confirms commit e34ab17 removed the second `state_hash(&canonical) != snapshot.hash` check from `restore`/`restore_report` and replaced it with the `RestoreReport.canonical_changed` migration signal, exactly as claimed; the CHANGELOG's "快照檔格式版本與遷移" section states this trade-off in the same words the finding quotes.
- `crates/interaction-runtime/src/character_session.rs:579` (`CharacterSessionHost::open`) does call `restore_report` and, on `needs_migration()==true`, takes `Startup::Migrate`, accepting the session rather than rejecting/quarantining — this is the real daemon boot path, not a hypothetical caller.
- All file:line citations (message.rs:94, session.rs 198/288-293/319-345, character_session.rs:579) check out exactly against current file content — no line drift.
- `cargo test -p interaction-session --test state_hash_fixtures` and `-p interaction-aip --test conformance` both pass, confirming the finding's claim that no existing fixture covers "unknown key nested inside members[].party".

Where I partially disagree with the finding is the severity/impact framing, not the existence of the bug. The finding's evidence quotes the design-intent comment "被污染的 state 若原樣還原，會被當成權威狀態重新廣播給所有成員" as the disaster this enables — but my own reproduction shows that is exactly what does NOT happen: `restored members[0].party = {"id":"desktop","kind":"human-surface"}`, i.e. `evilKey` is silently dropped, not carried through. The very next sentence of that same code comment (session.rs) explicitly names this as the actual safety net: "落地的權威狀態永遠是 canonical..., 所以就算某個鍵溜過檢查也不會被重新廣播出去." So the specific catastrophic outcome alleged (attacker-controlled unknown content reaching other members as authoritative state) is not real; the actual defect is narrower: a snapshot with foreign/unknown nested content that *should* trip the "未知欄位一律拒絕" quarantine/reject path instead gets silently accepted as a normal migration (`canonical_changed=true`, no distinguishing store note per the CHANGELOG's "遷移不是重建...不寫 storeNote"), so an operator cannot tell "old-format file" apart from "file had foreign content stripped." That's a real defense-in-depth / observability gap and a genuine contradiction of the documented invariant, worth fixing (e.g. add `deny_unknown_fields` to `Party`, or an explicit allowed-keys check analogous to `attention_keys_are_known`), but it does not rise to the "high" severity implied by "polluted state gets rebroadcast to all members" — that specific harm is already prevented by the canonical-only broadcast design the same file documents. I'm downgrading to medium: real, reproducible, exploitable only by someone who already has write access to the local session-state file (who could otherwise just tamper with legitimate fields directly to equal or greater effect), and whose actual consequence is silent accept-instead-of-quarantine, not data exfiltration/injection into the broadcast state.

confirmed.fix: 最小修法：比照 attention_keys_are_known 的做法，在反序列化 SemanticState 之前，對 snapshot.state 的每個 `members[*].party` 物件做一次允許鍵白名單檢查（只允許 kind／id），檔在 attention_keys_are_known 旁邊、restore_report 的同一組前置檢查裡；或者更直接地替 Party 加上 `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`——但 Party 也被 Envelope.source/target、CapabilityAnnouncement 等『線上』訊息型別共用，加下去之前要先確認 AIP 的 envelope 解析路徑沒有依賴 Party 對未知鍵寬容（forward-compat）；如果有，就只在 interaction-session 這一層另開一個嚴格版 PartyStrict/wrapper 型別供 MemberView 用，而不是動到共用的 wire-level Party。無論哪種修法，都應該補一支對照 restore_rejects_a_sign_negative_zero_intensity 風格的回歸測試：塞 members[].party 未知鍵的 tampered snapshot 必須回 SessionError::InvalidState。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified by direct code tracing plus a throwaway integration test run against the actual runtime (created, run, then deleted; repo confirmed clean via `git status --short` afterward — no lingering changes).

Mechanism, confirmed line-for-line in this branch's new code:
- `declarative_session.rs` is a wholly new file in this branch (didn't exist at base 8f52837 — `git show 8f52837:...declarative_session.rs` errors with "path does not exist").
- `declaration_for_spec` (declarative_session.rs:69-88) sets `declaration_id = provider_id`, so each declarative device is its own "family" for capability-declaration purposes.
- `transition_provider` (providers.rs:1262-1288, also new in this diff) calls `disable_provider_capabilities` + `stop_provider_sensing` for every `provider_stopped(state)`, and `provider_stopped` (interaction-registry/src/providers.rs:23-31) includes `Disabled`, not just `Revoked`/`Closed`/`Expired`.
- `stop_provider_sensing` (sensor_source.rs:428-454) unconditionally calls `source.release(...)`, which for `DeclarativeSensorSource` (declarative_session.rs:545-583) calls `retire()`, which unconditionally calls `rt.retract_provider_capabilities(&self.provider_id)` (line 570) — with no branch distinguishing "temporarily disabled" from "permanently revoked."
- Re-enabling (`transition_provider(..., Available)`) never re-declares the capability nor re-calls `bind_declarative_device`; the code even documents this is deliberate ("反方向刻意不做…自動打開會默默推翻人類的決定") — but that comment is about *enabling receptor/actuator flags*, not about *re-registering the capability declaration itself*, which is a distinct and seemingly unintended casualty.
- This directly contradicts the doc comment the same diff adds at providers.rs:480-495 on `declare_provider_capabilities`/`retract_provider_capabilities`: retract is documented as being for when "整族不再存在" (the whole family no longer exists), explicitly contrasted with "撤銷一支手機不會讓 iphone.mic-level 從此不再是高風險受器" (revoking one device should not retract a still-existing family's semantics). For declarative devices, `Disabled` (not gone, not revoked, family very much still exists) triggers exactly the retraction the doc says should be reserved for family-extinction.

Live-tested proof (scratch test, run once, then deleted):
```
declaration present BEFORE disable: true
declaration present WHILE disabled: false
registry.receptor() error while disabled: Some("unavailable: receptor desk-light.status is disabled")
provider descriptor state after re-enable: Available
declaration present AFTER re-enable (no restart): false
registry.receptor() error after re-enable: Some("unavailable: receptor desk-light.status is disabled")
set_receptor_enabled(true) result after re-enable: Ok(())
registry.receptor() after manual re-enable: is_ok=true
```
This proves the exact gap claimed: `GET /v1/providers/{id}` reports `Available` while `capability_declarations_report()` (backing `/v1/providers/declarations`) still omits the device, with no restart having happened.

No existing test covers this window: `a_disabled_declarative_device_stays_off_until_a_human_enables_it_again` (tests/providers_loop.rs:761) only checks the receptor-enabled flag across a restart cycle; `re_enabling_a_provider_never_re_arms_its_capabilities` (tests/providers_loop.rs:1718) uses a bare fake provider with no registered `SensorSource`/capability declaration at all, so it never exercises `declarative_session.rs`'s retire/retract path. `the_declaration_table_has_a_read_only_projection` (tests/providers_loop.rs:1765) never touches disable/enable. So the specific mismatch is real and untested.

One correction to the finding's evidence: the claim "它的受器在 registry 裡仍是 NotFound" is factually wrong. My test shows the receptor descriptor stays registered — `registry.receptor()` returns `Unavailable("... is disabled")`, not `NotFound`, and `set_receptor_enabled(true)` succeeds afterward (which would fail with NotFound if the descriptor were truly gone). `disable_provider_capabilities` (providers.rs) only flips `enabled=false` via `set_receptor_enabled`; it never calls `unregister_receptor`. So the receptor-registry part of the evidence is inaccurate — "disabled/Unavailable", not "NotFound" — but this doesn't undermine the core claim, which is about the capability-declarations report and SensorSource registration (both of which genuinely are absent/None during the window), and is independently confirmed.

Overall: this is a real, newly-introduced (this branch) state/capability-declaration inconsistency during the Disabled→Available (pre-restart) window, contradicting the very doc comment the branch itself adds, and not covered by any test. Consequence is bounded to observability/consistency (nothing pretends to operate — the receptor is still functionally gated off since its `enabled` flag isn't restored either), matching the finding's own "medium" framing.

3. `BuiltinAdapterMeta` (adapterRegistry.ts:80-127) has no scene-related field at all (no `scenes`, no `hasScene`) — confirmed by reading the full interface. `builtinAdapterMeta()` (adapterRegistry.ts:260-262) returns exactly that type, so `settingsTransfer.ts` has no capability query surface to bind `companionScene` to even if it wanted to. `scene` is declared only inside `shu.ts`'s CPP `capabilities()` map (line 186) — a different, unrelated mechanism (protocol-level capability advertisement, not `BuiltinAdapterMeta`). `rg` over sprite.ts/text.ts/shape.ts confirms zero mentions of "scene".

4. `exportCompanionSettings` (57-80) has `keepPersona`/`keepFamiliars` bound to `meta`, but no `keepScene` — `companionScene` is written unconditionally (line 73) regardless of target adapter.

5. Reran `pnpm vitest run src/test/playfield.test.ts` (19/19 pass, current HEAD). The cited test (lines 261-268) calls `parseCompanionSettingsImport({kind, schemaVersion:1, companionScene:"night", totallyUnknown:123})` with **no** `companionPack` and **no** `entrypointFor` — `ok.companionScene` is `"night"`, proving the field is accepted with zero character binding, exactly as the finding claims. This is not a case the branch's own tests treat as a regression; it passes as designed.

6. Not just a crafted-JSON corner case: `companionScene` (desktop.ts:44) is a persistent `DesktopPrefs` field with no reset-on-character-switch logic found anywhere in the app (`rg` for reset logic returns nothing), and `adapterReconfigureFor` (gatewayWiring.ts:415-424) unconditionally forwards `scene: prefs?.companionScene ?? "none"` to every adapter's reconfigure payload (also in `LIVE_PREF_KEYS`) regardless of whether that adapter understands scenes — so a normal switch-character-then-export flow (no hand-editing needed) can carry a shu-specific scene value into a file tagged for a scene-less character, and it round-trips silently.

7. Checked scope claims: the branch's own progress doc (`docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md` row 2.4/§3.4) and CHANGELOG both describe this wave's fix as binding `variants`/`personas`/`hasPlayfield` — `companionScene` was never in the stated scope and known-limitation #17's original v0.6.0 wording only named the familiars-palette case. So the finding's framing that M2 §3.4 "should have" covered scene is somewhat an extrapolation rather than a broken promise, but the underlying technical claim (scene remains a global whitelist with no adapter-meta binding, unlike persona/familiars fixed in this exact diff) is fully accurate and is a real, currently-live completeness gap in the same bug class the diff's own header comment (lines 8-13) describes and claims to eliminate. Medium severity: no security/safety-invariant breach (doesn't leak revision/token/uuid, doesn't touch consent/estop), but it's a genuine, reproducible architecture-boundary gap left half-fixed by this branch's flagship change.</reasoning>

verdicts.reasoning:
Core mechanism claim verified by reading the code: register_device_outbound (character_session.rs:859-880) has no identity-strength/transport check — table.insert() unconditionally overwrites any existing entry for a device_id, and both mobile.rs:3329 (paired-token) and declarative_session.rs:172/note_ready (transport-hello+device-side-pairing) write into the same BTreeMap keyed by the bare id string. bind_identity only checks envelope.source == party, never whether that id is already claimed elsewhere at higher strength. This part is real and reproducible.

However the finding's exploit narrative rests on a factual error: it cites `interact-ai character adapters add` (routes to POST /v1/character/adapters, the Character Presentation Protocol external-renderer registration in character_ws.rs) as the attacker's entry point for creating a hostile Serial/MQTT/BLE device with a colliding expectedDeviceId. That subsystem never touches register_device_outbound, PartyKind::Device, or expectedDeviceId — it's unrelated. The actual mechanism for adding a declarative device spec (config/adapters/*.yaml) has no HTTP/CLI endpoint at all: it is read exactly once, at providers.rs:534 init_providers(), called only once from runtime.rs:455 during daemon construction (confirmed no file watcher exists). Reaching the attack therefore requires local filesystem write access to ~/.adaptive-interaction/config/adapters/ — the same home tree holding state/api-token (config.rs:14/98, 0600, same OS user) — plus a full daemon restart. That level of access already equals or exceeds holding the Bearer token itself (an attacker there could just read the token and do far worse directly), so the described attack does not cross a genuine privilege boundary in this single-user local-daemon threat model; the code comment at providers.rs even labels these files "File=Truth; human-owned specs," i.e. already-trusted input.

Net: the code-level gap (no cross-transport identity-strength check before overwriting the outbound registry) is a real, worth-fixing defense-in-depth issue, but it is not the high-severity, operator-reachable privilege-escalation the finding describes — the cited attacker capability (character adapters CLI) cannot produce the scenario, and the real path requires already-equivalent-to-full-compromise local access.

The code-level fact is real: `register_device_outbound` (character_session.rs:859-879) only checks `MAX_DEVICE_OUTBOUND` fullness and unconditionally `table.insert`s over an existing key, with no comparison of the incoming channel's `identity_strength()` against whatever is already registered for that `device_id`; `declarative_session.rs`'s `note_ready` (:154-186) calls it on every successful handshake with the spec's `expectedDeviceId`, and `interaction-session::join` (session.rs:455-483) matches purely on `Party` equality with zero transport/identity awareness by design (it's a pure, transport-agnostic crate). This part of the finding is confirmed as written.

Where the finding fails is the exploit chain and severity. Two factual problems:

1. The finding's cited enabling mechanism — "`interact-ai character adapters add` 的合法操作者權限" — is wrong. That CLI subcommand (main.rs:763-772, `CharacterAdapterAction::Add`) registers an *external Character Presentation Protocol adapter* (a WebSocket renderer, sha256-token based, revocable) — a completely different subsystem from declarative hardware devices (Serial/MQTT/BLE specs under `config/adapters/*.yaml`, owned by `interaction-adapter-declarative`/`providers.rs`). There is no CLI or HTTP surface that lets any operator — privileged or not — add or hot-reload a declarative device spec at runtime; `providers.rs:444/534` and `runtime.rs:455` show declarative adapters are loaded exactly once, from disk, during `Runtime::new`'s `init_providers()`. To exploit this, an attacker needs to place a crafted YAML file under `~/.adaptive-interaction/config/adapters/` *before or at daemon startup* — there is no lower-privilege API-driven path.

2. Given that required capability, the 'attacker' already holds a strictly stronger position than the legitimate human operator, not a weaker one. `config/adapters/` and `state/api-token` are siblings under the same home directory (`Paths` in config.rs), with no directory-level privilege separation anywhere in the codebase (only the token *files* get `0o600`, not a distinct owner/group for the config tree). Anyone able to write into `config/adapters/*.yaml` before/at daemon start, in this single-user desktop architecture, can trivially also read `state/api-token` and call the HTTP API directly with full human authority — which lets them do strictly more than hijacking one device's outbound channel (submit any action, drive the session as any role through the legitimate join path, etc.), without touching this code path at all. CLAUDE.md's Bearer-token / loopback model exists to separate AI-agent scope from human scope and to keep the API off the network, not to wall off 'whoever can write local config files' from 'whoever holds the token' — no such boundary is documented or enforced. So the scenario is not a privilege escalation in this system's actual threat model; it needs full local compromise to begin with, and at that point the outbound-registry overwrite is redundant to capabilities the attacker already has.

Net: this is a real (if narrow) architectural gap — register_device_outbound doesn't defend against an accidental or malicious device_id collision across transports, and a bad actor/misconfiguration could silently steal a device's channel with no audit distinction — but it does not clear 'high' as a security finding because (a) its evidence misattributes an unrelated CLI feature as the enabling mechanism, and (b) the actual required capability already subsumes the full local trust boundary, making it non-exploitable as a cross-privilege attack. I'd log this as a low-severity hardening/defense-in-depth item (reject or audit-with-distinction when a device_id is already registered under a different/stronger identity_strength) rather than a confirmed high-severity vulnerability.
